page: Microsoft Azure M32bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The configuration includes 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity stands at 256.0 GB, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage is bundled with a local 410 GB SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in specific single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. The server achieves strong results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, alongside strong performance in gzip compression and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth is measured at 2766.64 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 181.54 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. While small-model LLM text generation is strong at 312.22 tokens/sec, large-model LLM text generation is weak, registering at 2.74 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M32bds_v3 offers a dense memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound workloads without requiring the expense of a GPU. However, the lack of hardware accelerators limits its utility for heavy deep learning tasks, as evidenced by the low large-model LLM inference speeds. The server is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving.
